newsitem.title: GERMANY: SNB's Meyer stands by Swiss monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Meyer stands by Swiss monetary policy.

text.p: Swiss National Bank president Hans Meyer said on Tuesday evening that the Swiss central bank would stick by its current monetary policy and consider a change when appropriate.
Speaking to journalists in Frankfurt, the SNB chief also said that he was not displeased with the current Swiss franc/mark exchange rate, which he said showed the success of Swiss monetary policies.
Turning to Europe's monetary union, Meyer said that while he welcomed the project, it would not be disastrous if the euro currency failed to get off the ground.
"The present situation is not bad, we can live with it," Meyer said.
Switzerland had several options on how to approach the euro, Meyer said. The country could either peg the Swiss franc to another currency or try to maintain a degree of flexibility.
The decisive factor would be which way would better guarantee stable monetary policy, he said.
Meyer said he expected muted economic development in Switzerland in 1997, but a more positive development in 1998.
